content.question_html:
A researcher wants to test whether listening to music affects how many words people can recall from a list.

(a)
Write a suitable hypothesis for this study.
(2)
(b)
Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable.
(2)
content.mark_scheme_html:
(a)
A clear, testable statement that includes both conditions and the measured outcome
(2)

e.g. There will be a difference in the number of words recalled by participants who learn with music and participants who learn in silence.

(b)
Independent variable: whether music is played
(1)
Dependent variable: the number of words recalled

content.question_html:
Describe and evaluate Piaget's theory of cognitive development.
(9)
content.mark_scheme_html:
Marked by level of response. Top-level answers are detailed, well organised and reach a supported judgement.

Indicative content:

  • Schemas, assimilation and accommodation
  • Four stages: sensorimotor, pre-operational, concrete operational and formal operational
  • Evaluation: influential in education; later research suggests children can do more at younger ages; the samples were small and from one culture

content.question_html:
Describe and evaluate Asch's study of conformity.
(9)
content.mark_scheme_html:
Marked by level of response. Top-level answers are detailed, well organised and reach a supported judgement.

Indicative content:

  • Line judgement task with confederates giving wrong answers
  • About one third of responses on critical trials conformed; most participants conformed at least once
  • Evaluation: controlled laboratory study; an artificial task; a sample of American male students in the 1950s; ethical issues of deception

content.question_html:
Explain how cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT) is used to treat depression, and give one strength of this therapy.
(6)
content.mark_scheme_html:
The therapist helps the patient to identify negative, irrational thoughts
(1)
These thoughts are challenged and replaced with more rational ones
(1)
Behavioural activation: the patient plans and carries out enjoyable activities
(1)
Homework such as thought diaries is completed between sessions
(1)
Strength: it gives patients skills to manage future episodes, with a lower relapse rate
